purpose: Reference notes for visual road-condition classification. These definitions guide model prompts; they are not labeled training images.

condition_levels.definition: The visible drivable pavement is continuous and reasonably even, with no clearly visible active defect. Do not call a road new based on an image.
The road remains mostly continuous but has limited cracks, small repairs, early wear, or isolated low-severity defects.
One or more clearly visible potholes, broad deformation, connected alligator cracking, severe material loss, or multiple defects materially affect the visible pavement.
The drivable road surface is absent, too small, blocked, blurred, dark, overexposed, or otherwise not clear enough to assess.

defects.definition: A narrow crack running mainly in the direction of travel, often parallel to the lane or pavement edge.
defects.visual_cues: A visible split in the pavement surface with a lengthwise orientation.
defects.avoid_confusing_with: Lane paint, a sealed construction joint, tar seams, shadows, or tire marks.

defects.definition: A crack crossing mainly across the direction of travel.
defects.visual_cues: A distinct line that cuts across much of the visible lane.
defects.avoid_confusing_with: Painted lane markings, expansion joints, crosswalks, or image compression.

defects.definition: A connected network of small polygonal cracks, commonly resembling scales or a mesh.
defects.visual_cues: Several interlinked cracks forming repeated small polygons over a pavement area.
defects.avoid_confusing_with: A few isolated cracks, road markings, cobblestones, or naturally patterned pavement.

defects.definition: A localized cavity or missing pavement material with a visible rim, broken surface, or recessed appearance.
defects.visual_cues: An irregular bounded break in the road surface; surrounding broken edges strengthen the evidence.
defects.avoid_confusing_with: A dark shadow, puddle, manhole cover, patch, or painted marking. Do not infer depth from a monocular image.

defects.definition: A localized area of replaced or repaired pavement with a visible material or texture boundary.
defects.visual_cues: A bounded area with a different texture, color, or seam, often rectangular or irregular.
defects.avoid_confusing_with: An open pothole. A patch is evidence of repair and is not automatically an active defect.

defects.definition: Longitudinal depressions or grooves in the wheel paths.
defects.visual_cues: Parallel shallow channels or raised edges following vehicle wheel paths over distance.
defects.avoid_confusing_with: Perspective, lighting bands, tire marks, or a road crown. Without depth sensing, describe only visible shape.

defects.definition: A visible localized sag, bulge, settlement, or uneven pavement profile that is not a distinct pothole.
defects.visual_cues: A change in pavement plane, displaced surface, or uneven patch boundary.
defects.avoid_confusing_with: Normal road camber, perspective, moving shadows, or vehicle motion blur.

defects.definition: A visibly rough, porous, or fragmenting pavement surface with aggregate or material loss.
defects.visual_cues: A rough area with small exposed aggregate or a visibly deteriorated texture.
defects.avoid_confusing_with: Normal coarse asphalt texture, gravel shoulders, dirt, or image noise.

defects.definition: Broken or missing pavement along the road edge, often where the paved surface meets a shoulder.
defects.visual_cues: A fractured, crumbling, or missing strip at the pavement boundary.
defects.avoid_confusing_with: An intentionally unpaved shoulder or a normal pavement edge.

defects.definition: A visible pavement defect that does not fit the named classes.
defects.visual_cues: Use only when a specific surface irregularity is visible and the defined classes do not fit.
defects.avoid_confusing_with: Road furniture, debris, vehicles, stains, or objects that are not pavement damage.

review_rules: Classify only the visible drivable pavement, not sidewalks, buildings, vehicles, or vegetation.
If evidence is ambiguous, use not_assessable or type other with low confidence; do not invent a defect.
Good means no defect is visible in this frame, not that the entire street or road is certified safe.
Do not infer pavement age, defect depth, physical size, repair priority, or structural cause from one monocular frame.
Severity is a visual estimate for human review, never a measured engineering rating.
